task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 20, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper update about the delayed maintenance hangar at Rookmeadow Airport and the business decisions waiting on its construction.

facts.text: Rookmeadow Airport Authority said Thursday, Aug. 20, 2026, that the start of its proposed maintenance-hangar construction will be delayed at least three months.
The authority had planned to begin site work in September and open the hangar in May 2027.
The drainage permit is incomplete because the engineering submission omitted runoff calculations for an adjacent service apron.
The permit office requested the missing calculations on July 29; it has not rejected the entire project.
The hangar project's approved capital budget is $7.2 million, including an estimated $420,000 for site drainage.
The authority has not priced the additional drainage design or revised the final construction budget.
Prospective tenant Finchward Aviation has paid a refundable $120,000 lease deposit.
Its agreement allows withdrawal if the hangar is not available by Sept. 1, 2027; the company has not exercised that option.
Finchward's current workshop is at another airport, and it plans to keep operating there during the delay.
The company projected 40 jobs at the new site, including 24 transfers and 16 additional positions, conditional on opening.
Those positions are not all new regional jobs, and no new-site hiring notices have been issued.
A technical-college placement program had expected six trainee rotations at the new hangar next summer.
The college is seeking alternative placements but has not canceled the trainees' course.
Finchward manager Rella Vint said, "We can keep repairing aircraft where we are. We cannot recruit against a building date that keeps moving."
Neighboring garden-center owner Tavin Lark said he supports the jobs but wants drainage settled before more hard surface is built.
Lark said, "A permit question can be paperwork at the airport and water at my fence."
The reporting record does not establish that the proposed hangar has caused flooding at the garden center.
The airport's existing passenger and freight services will continue; the delay concerns the new maintenance facility.
The proposed hangar site has been used for equipment storage since a taxiway realignment in 2011.
The authority will publish a revised schedule after receiving the drainage engineer's submission, with no specific publication date promised.
